facts.claim: The A380 entered service in 2007; the A350 made its first flight in June 2013 and the A350-900 entered commercial service with Qatar Airways in January 2015.

The A380 has eight main flight-deck displays plus Onboard Information System screens; the A350 uses six identical large-format displays sharing one part number, fully interchangeable in hardware and software.

The A350 replaced the MCDU workflow with Keyboard and Cursor Control Units (KCCUs), a concept introduced on the A380; in December 2019 China Eastern received the first A350 with optional touchscreen displays, with three of the six displays touch-capable.

The A380 hosted 23 flight-system functions on shared processing modules while the A350's second-generation IMA can consolidate up to 40; the A350 uses 18 data-network switches versus 16 on the A380, and refined the A380's two-hydraulic/two-electrical (2H2E) architecture.

Cross Crew Qualification is available for A320 Family, A340 and A380 pilots with training reduced by up to 78%; the course takes 11 days for A320 Family, 10 days for A340 and five days for A380 pilots, and A330 pilots can qualify for the A350 without mandatory Full Flight Simulator time with about 60% less training than a full type-rating course.
A380 production ended with the final delivery in 2021; Qantas plans to begin retiring its A380s in fiscal year 2032 while introducing A350-1000s.

zh.title: A350駕駛艙其實源自A380：六面大螢幕、KCCU與整合航電的傳承
zh.summary: 空中巴士A350駕駛艙看似全新世代，實則以A380駕駛艙為起點重新設計：六面可互換大螢幕、鍵盤游標控制單元、第二代整合模組航電與2H2E架構皆源自超級巨無霸的經驗，並讓跨機型轉訓大幅縮短。
body: 空中巴士A380或許正逐步退出各航空公司機隊，但它最重要的設計概念之一，仍在每一次A350起飛時出現在飛行員面前。A350駕駛艙並非縮小版的A380駕駛艙：六面大螢幕、不同的操控系統與更簡潔的配置，讓它看來像是全新世代；但空中巴士刻意以A380概念為起點，把其中最重要的想法帶進A350。A380於2007年投入服務，A350於2013年6月首飛、2015年1月隨卡達航空投入商業服務，空中巴士得以在數年實際營運經驗後重新設計介面，而非單純複製。

最明顯的差異在螢幕數量與運用方式。A380有8面主顯示器，另有機載資訊系統螢幕；A350改用6面規格相同的大型顯示器，空中巴士表示6面螢幕共用同一料號，硬體與軟體皆可完全互換。資訊不再固定於某一面實體螢幕，而是可在駕駛艙內重新配置；顯示器故障時系統可自動重組航電頁面，外側螢幕故障的資訊也能在他處恢復。主飛行顯示器在主要畫面下方增加襟翼與配平等資訊，導航顯示器可提供航路與地形的垂直剖面；推力顯示則沿用A380導入的簡化百分比概念，而非回到N1與EPR分開顯示的舊制。

介面本身也隨之改變。A350以鍵盤與游標控制單元（KCCU）取代傳統多功能控制顯示單元（MCDU）的操作方式：飛行員不再各自受限於附小螢幕的MCDU，而是以KCCU操控整片大型顯示器，游標可在欄位與螢幕之間移動。KCCU的概念其實源自A380，A350則把它推向核心；2019年12月，中國東方航空接收首架配備選配觸控螢幕的A350，6面顯示器中有3面可觸控，分別為兩面外側螢幕與下方中央顯示器。螢幕之下是整合模組航電（IMA）：A380可在共用處理模組上搭載23項飛航系統功能，A350第二代IMA可整合至多40項，資料網路交換器也由16具增至18具；液壓與電力架構則沿用A380的2H2E概念，即兩套液壓與兩套電路。

傳承的實質回報在訓練與機隊運用。空中巴士表示，A320系列、A340與A380飛行員可透過跨機型資格（CCQ）轉訓A350，訓練時間最多縮短78%；A330與A350飛行員則可依共同型別檢定安排執飛。據先前報導，CCQ課程A320系列飛行員需11天、A340飛行員10天、A380飛行員僅5天；A330飛行員轉訓A350甚至無需強制全動式模擬機時間，訓練時間較完整型別檢定課程減少約60%。A380生產已於2021年最終交付後結束，澳洲航空則計畫自2032財政年度起退役A380、同時引進A350-1000；對轉訓的飛行員而言，兩代駕駛艙的邏輯仍將相通。

en.title: The Airbus A350 cockpit shares its DNA with the A380: six displays, KCCUs and integrated avionics
en.summary: The Airbus A350 flight deck looks like a new generation, but it was designed from the A380 cockpit as its starting point: six interchangeable large displays, keyboard and cursor control units, second-generation integrated modular avionics and the 2H2E architecture all carry the superjumbo's lessons forward, sharply cutting cross-crew training time.
body: The Airbus A380 may be disappearing from airline fleets, but one of its most important ideas still sits in front of pilots every time an A350 leaves the ground. The A350 flight deck does not look like a smaller version of the superjumbo's cockpit: six large displays, a different control system and a cleaner layout make it look like a newer generation altogether. Airbus deliberately started with the A380 concept and carried several of its most important ideas into the A350. The A380 entered service in 2007, giving Airbus several years of operational experience with a highly integrated widebody flight deck before the A350 made its first flight in June 2013; the A350-900 then entered commercial service with Qatar Airways in January 2015.

The biggest visual difference is also the clearest sign that Airbus refined rather than copied its earlier design. The A380 has eight main flight-deck displays, plus additional screens for its Onboard Information System, while the A350 uses six identical large-format displays. Airbus says all six share the same part number and are fully interchangeable in hardware and software. Information can be rearranged across the flight deck instead of being tied to a particular physical screen, and if a display fails the system can automatically reconfigure the avionics pages. The primary flight display adds information such as flap and trim indications below the main presentation, the navigation display can show a vertical profile of the route and terrain, and the thrust presentation follows the simplified percentage-based philosophy introduced with the A380 rather than returning to the older split between N1 and EPR indications.

The interface itself changed too. The A350's Keyboard and Cursor Control Units (KCCUs) replace the traditional Multifunction Control and Display Unit (MCDU) workflow: instead of each pilot being tied to an MCDU with its own small screen, the KCCU lets the crew interact with the larger cockpit displays, with the cursor moving between fields and screens. The concept itself came from the A380, which introduced KCCUs to control new functions; the A350 made them central. In December 2019, China Eastern Airlines received the first A350 equipped with optional touchscreen cockpit displays; Airbus says three of the six displays can be touch-capable — the two outer screens and the lower-center display. Underneath sits Integrated Modular Avionics (IMA): the A380 could host 23 flight-system functions on shared processing modules, while the A350's second-generation IMA can consolidate up to 40, and the A350 uses 18 data-network switches compared with 16 on the A380. The hydraulic and electrical architecture follows the same logic: the A380 uses two hydraulic and two electrical circuits, and the A350 refined that 2H2E philosophy.

The payoff shows in training and fleet use. Airbus says Cross Crew Qualification is available for A320 Family, A340 and A380 pilots, with training duration reduced by up to 78%, and A330 and A350 pilots can operate under a Common Type Rating arrangement. The cross-crew qualification course takes 11 days for A320 Family pilots, 10 days for A340 pilots and five days for A380 pilots, while A330 pilots can qualify for the A350 without mandatory Full Flight Simulator time, with training time reduced by around 60% compared with a full type-rating course. A380 production ended with its final delivery in 2021, and Qantas plans to begin retiring its A380s in fiscal year 2032 while introducing A350-1000s — but the cockpit logic connecting the two generations will carry over.
